items.prose: Seventy-two hours of continuous hardwood firing raised the vertical stone stack to 960°C, driving carbon dioxide out of thirty tons of quarry limestone. The resulting snow-white calcium oxide quicklime yields premium building mortar upon slaking.

Pouring cold sump water too rapidly into five hundred pounds of fresh quicklime lumps triggered a violent exothermic steam eruption. Scalding 140°C alkaline lime milk geysered out of the slaking trough, blinding an apprentice who was operating without eye goggles.

Excessive forced-draft anthracite firing overheated the dolomitic stone charge to 1,250°C. The magnesium carbonate sintered into un-reactive 'dead-burned' periclase crystals that refused to hydrate, ruining the batch for masonry mortar but yielding refractory hearth lining.

Feeding green birch logs into the lower fireboxes choked the natural chimney draft. Pyrolysis soot coated the uncalcined limestone chunks in black greasy carbon, insulating the rock and leaving 45% unburnt limestone cores in the discharge hopper.

Fused calcium silicate slag caused the descending stone column to bridge across the kiln waist. Stoker crews had to break the glowing eight-ton hanging arch from below with twenty-foot steel rods; the sudden fall crushed the bottom iron discharge grate.

Slaked lime putty submerged under a six-inch water layer in cool, dark Cavern 4 matured for eighteen months. Sub-microscopic platelet crystals grew, imparting buttery plasticity and zero-shrinkage setting for delicate vault ceiling fresco plastering.

A roof drip into stacked burlap bags of pulverized quicklime initiated spontaneous atmospheric hydration. Internal bag temperature reached 220°C, igniting wooden storage pallets and filling the storeroom with choking alkaline dust.

A sudden nuclear winter barometric inversion reversed airflow through the external kiln exhaust chimney. Five hundred ppm carbon monoxide gas was pushed down into the adjacent laundry dormitory, sickening twenty-four workers before dampers could be slammed shut.
